top_signals.title: Stocks Waver Ahead of CPI, Bank Earnings; Aramco Hit By Houthis
top_signals.summary: US equity futures waver ahead of the latest CPI data and bank earnings. ASML boosts its sales outlook and warns that it may not be able to meet soaring AI demand in 2027 and 2028. Iran-backed Houthis launches attacks across Saudi Arabia, hitting Saudi Aramco’s headquarters. Russia strikes energy facilities in Ukraine. Jerek Kutylowski of DeepL speaks to Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie at the International AI Summit in Dublin. Christopher Hodge of Natixis joins "Bloomberg Brief" to look ahead to the inflation print. Stephen Biggar of Argus Research breaks down bank earnings with Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on deck. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Bullard Sees ‘Two Hikes and Hope’ From Federal Reserve
top_signals.summary: Former St. Louis Federal Reserve President James Bullard discusses his outlook for the Fed’s policy path through the end of the year on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: ACEA President & Mercedes CEO 'Welcomes' EU Deal with China on Hybrids
top_signals.summary: The President of the auto lobby ACEA Ola Källenius, who’s also the CEO of Mercedes-Benz Group, welcomed the recent deal to cap the imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles to the EU. He called for a level-playing field and the EU to increase its competitiveness. He spoke with Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook in Brussels. (Source: Bloomberg)
